intro: We have gathered real questions about our diploma courses, certification, contact information, and institutional content, so that any person, search engine, or AI agent can find direct answers on a single page.

queOfrece.respuesta: The public website of AMMAC — the Montessori Association of Mexico (Asociación Montessori de México A.C.), founded in 1965 — brings together institutional information about diploma courses, certifications, publications, faculty profiles, contact details, and open resources related to Montessori training.

modalidad.pregunta: Are the diploma courses online or in person?
modalidad.respuesta: The diploma courses featured on the site are designed as online programs. The public content explains that you can study from anywhere in the world, with mentorship from course instructors and access to a digital learning platform.

certificacion.pregunta: What certification do I receive upon completion?
certificacion.respuesta: The site's public offering states that the programs include international Montessori certification issued by AMMAC and are designed to train you as a Montessori Guide. Specific details can be found on the Diploma Courses page.

equipoDocente.pregunta: Who is on the teaching team?
equipoDocente.respuesta: The faculty section of the diploma course presents public profiles such as Roxana Muñoz, Iván López Carmona, and Carlos Romero, with information about their background, training, and role within the program.

temas.pregunta: What subjects are studied in the diploma courses?
temas.respuesta: The site lists subjects such as Montessori Philosophy, Observation Methods, Neuroeducation, Educational Psychology, Music Therapy, Psychomotor Development, Inclusive Education, and Creative Intelligence, along with hands-on work with Montessori materials and presentations, all organized into a structure of work blocks.

estructuraPedagogica.pregunta: How is the training structured pedagogically?
estructuraPedagogica.respuesta: The entire training program is organized into seven competency domains (D1 through D7), developed with reference to the international domains of Montessori training (MACTE / AMI) and to AMI foundations: Philosophical and Historical Foundations; Human Development and the Planes of Development; The Prepared Environment and the Materials; Scientific Observation; Role and Transformation of the Adult (the Guide); Pedagogy of the Curriculum Areas; and Community, Family, and Leadership. Each domain is developed across the six cognitive levels of Bloom's Taxonomy (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, and Create).

estandaresAmi.pregunta: Is the diploma course aligned with international standards and AMI?
estandaresAmi.respuesta: Yes. The program is aligned with the international standards of Montessori training and is compatible with the foundations of AMI (Association Montessori Internationale). In addition, every activity has a learning objective coded as "Domain·Level" (for example, D1·Analyze): the domain indicates the area of competency, and the level, drawn from Bloom's Taxonomy, indicates the cognitive depth to be developed, so that every task has an explicit, assessable learning purpose.

documentos.pregunta: What documents are required for the certificate?
documentos.respuesta: The Diploma Courses page states that, for your international certificate, you will be asked to provide proof of address, official identification, a birth certificate, and your most recent academic certificate.

informes.pregunta: How can I request more information or get in touch?
informes.respuesta: You can write to admin@certificacionmontessori.com, call 55 5515 2701, or reach out on WhatsApp at 55 4888 5013. WhatsApp support is available from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., chat only.

ubicacion.pregunta: Where is the Asociación Montessori de México located?
ubicacion.respuesta: The public address shown on the site is Avenida Dos 48, San Pedro de los Pinos, Benito Juárez, 03800 Mexico City, Mexico.
